subskill: Line-parabola system: sum of the y-coordinates of intersections
prompt: In the xy-plane, the graph of y = 2x^2 + x - 5 intersects the graph of y = 3x + 7 at two points. What is the sum of the y-coordinates of the two points?
explanation: Set the expressions equal: 2x^2 + x - 5 = 3x + 7, so 2x^2 - 2x - 12 = 0, or x^2 - x - 6 = 0. The sum of the solutions is 1 (the solutions are x = 3 and x = -2). Each intersection point lies on the line, so its y-coordinate is 3x + 7. The sum of the y-coordinates is 3(x1 + x2) + 7 + 7 = 3(1) + 14 = 17. (Check: the points are (3, 16) and (-2, 1), and 16 + 1 = 17.) The value 1 is the sum of the x-coordinates, not the y-coordinates. The value 11 comes from a sign error in the sum of the solutions, using -1 instead of 1, so 3(-1) + 14 = 11. The value 20 comes from taking the sum of the solutions of 2x^2 - 2x - 12 = 0 to be 2 without dividing by the leading coefficient, so 3(2) + 14 = 20.
